# Finly

Finly is Bruce Wen's solo submission to the Alpaca AI Trading Agents Hackathon. It is an educational paper-trading research prototype, not investment advice.

## Judge-facing proposition

Finly separates market interpretation from capital-bearing authority. An AI component may assess a bounded evidence bundle, explain uncertainty, respond to evidence-removal challenges, and veto. Deterministic code owns exposure, horizon, defined-risk option construction, exact maximum loss, broker fields, and the final PERMIT or NO_TRADE decision. Broker mutation is disabled in the published evidence path.

## Release-gated quantitative findings

In the consumed, post-selected 2013-01-02–2026-08-27 retrospective replay with modeled 5 bp one-way costs, G4 returned +967.11% versus SPY +580.82%; promotion was rejected because the Deflated Sharpe probability was 3.75% and the worst familywise-adjusted p-value was 37.18%.

Production v1 is the frozen unlevered SPY/BIL policy targeting 10% annualized volatility: in the consumed 2025-01-02–2026-08-28 modeled next-open study it returned +15.39% at 5 bp per traded leg and +10.56% at 25 bp, versus SPY +33.52%; at 5 bp its modeled annualized volatility was 8.12% and maximum drawdown was -5.45%, so it was risk-controlled but not market-beating on total return.

Attempts 115 and 116 are publicly registered future-only tests. As of 2026-08-30T08:10:52.000Z, each had zero observed outcomes, and neither supports a performance claim.

## Evidence boundary

G4 is a rejected, post-selected research shadow—not the production policy. The historical studies are modeled ETF ledgers, not broker fills or options P&L. The future-only receipts are GitHub platform records, not independent cryptographic timestamps or outcome evidence. Finly does not claim future profitability, next-month SPY outperformance, a competitor rank, or a Finly-versus-competitor return matchup.

## Verification

From a clean clone with the release-pinned Node.js 26.7.0 runtime: `npm install && npm run verify`.

The release gate verifies seven source artifacts by hash. Hash verification establishes byte integrity; it is not independent validation of the underlying financial claims.
